hypotheses.justification: The other assumptions imply finiteness. If ι is empty, it is already finite. Otherwise choose j₀ and put t = conj φ s. Since n > 0 and t^[n] = id, t is a ring automorphism. In an arbitrary product of fields, the primitive nonzero idempotents are exactly the singleton indicators: coordinatewise, IsIdempotentElem.iff_eq_zero_or_one makes every idempotent a characteristic function, and any larger support contains a proper singleton idempotent. Automorphisms preserve this characterization. Thus each e_m = t^[m](ind {j₀}) is a singleton indicator. Set q = 1 - ∏ m ∈ Finset.range n, (1 - e_m). Coordinatewise q is idempotent; cycling the factors shows t q = q. The proof's hfix01 argument uses no finiteness, so q is 0 or 1. Its j₀-coordinate is 1, hence q = 1. Consequently the supports of these n singleton indicators cover ι, proving Finite ι. Install this derived instance and use the existing proof unchanged.
